version.changelog:
Initial release of openclaw-workspace-cleaner.

- Provides a structured process for optimizing core OpenClaw workspace files (AGENTS, MEMORY, SOUL, TOOLS, IDENTITY, USER)
- Requires listing and confirming an optimization plan before making changes, ensuring safety and user control
- Moves unused or redundant content to deep storage (memory/) and deletes obsolete files (like BOOTSTRAP.md)
- Adds daily journaling of each optimization for traceability
- Enforces strict boundaries: only affects the agent’s own workspace and files

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions are consistent with its stated purpose: it reads and edits local OpenClaw workspace bootstrap files to archive or delete unnecessary content, and it requests no credentials or external installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required artifacts, and declared requirements align: the skill aims to trim bootstrap/workspace files and its instructions are limited to manipulating files under the agent workspace. It does not request unrelated binaries, env vars, or network access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs reading and modifying local bootstrap files and archiving content into memory/; these actions are within scope. One mild ambiguity: it relies on the notion of '自己的工作区' (own workspace) but does not define how to deterministically identify which agent's workspace in multi-agent environments, so accidental cross-agent edits are possible if the agent runtime does not enforce that constraint.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install steps, downloads, or code to execute. Lowest installation risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or external config paths are required. All declared actions are local file operations, which are proportionate to the stated task.

dimensions.detail: Does not request always: true and is user-invocable. It does modify local files when confirmed, which is expected behavior for this type of utility.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent but will read and modify files in your local OpenClaw workspace (~/.openclaw/workspace). Before approving any action: 1) Inspect the optimization plan the skill lists and refuse execution until you understand every change; 2) Make a backup copy of your workspace (or run the skill on a copy) so deletions/archives can be recovered; 3) Confirm how the agent identifies 'your' workspace in multi-agent setups to avoid accidental edits to other agents; 4) Pay attention to the deletion of BOOTSTRAP.md and the archive append behavior (it appends to existing target files rather than replacing); 5) If you want stricter safety, ask the skill to output a dry-run showing exact file diffs before performing writes.
